text:
kai: Hi all — quick logistics q. My partner and I are expecting in Aug and we'll be listed as "domestic partners" on the paperwork. What's required to get partner-bonding leave, add the baby to benefits, and get the one-time new-child grant?

sam (People Ops): Congrats @kai! :tada: Short answers: you can apply for partner bonding (usually up to 12 weeks paid depending on tenure), you need to submit the parental leave request form + proof of birth (or hospital record) within 30 days for benefits enrollment, and the New Child Grant is a separate one-time taxable payment processed through payroll.

kai: Thanks. For proof of parentage, do we need a birth certificate? We're doing a home birth with midwife and may not have the certificate immediately.

toni (Benefits): Good q — birth certificate is ideal but not required immediately. Acceptable docs in the first 30 days: hospital or midwife birth record, signed affidavit from provider, or court docs for adoption. You must provide the official birth certificate within 60 days if available so benefits can keep the dependent on the plan. Link to dependent enrollment steps: https://benefits.redwood.com/new-dependent

kai: And for domestic partner status, any extra paperwork? We're not married.

sam (People Ops): We ask for a signed domestic partner declaration + proof of shared residence (one item) or joint financial doc (optional). If you already have partner on file from when you enrolled benefits, skip that step. If unsure, reply here and we can check your HR record.

amy (eng-manager): From a coverage side I'm happy to coordinate leave coverage. Kai ping me when you have dates and we'll map out priorities. We can do a 2-week handoff plan and temp coverage for on-call.

kai: Do I file for parental leave or a caregiver block? I plan to take 6 weeks after the birth then maybe 2 weeks later to help with paperwork.

sam (People Ops): Use the "Parental/Partner Leave" option in the request form for bonding after a birth. If you need intermittent days later, file a short-term caregiver request. For continuous bonding, include start/end dates; for intermittent, add notes on frequency. We coordinate with payroll for pay codes.

toni (Benefits): Enrollment note: add the baby to medical, dental, and dependent life within 30 days of birth. For flexible spending accounts, you can submit claims for eligible dependent care expenses retroactively. Also, Redwood's childcare subsidy is a separate program applied via People Ops — ask if you want that.

kai: What about the New Child Grant amount and timeline? Also is it automatic?

hr-bot: New Child Grant - summary: one-time taxable payment of $2,000 for birth/adoption/placement. Submit New Child Grant form linked from the parental leave form. Payroll processes on next monthly run after approval. If submitted after payroll cutoff, processed as off-cycle (allow 3 business days).

kai: Good to know. Anything else I should be aware of around performance reviews or probation if I'm out for a couple months?

sam (People Ops): We have a policy: time on parental leave does not negatively affect performance rating. Managers should document goals and check-ins pre/post leave. If you have a performance calibration during your leave window, we'll coordinate with your manager to consider context. For probation/extensions we evaluate on a case-by-case basis but parental leave itself is not used to extend probation.

amy (eng-manager): I'll write up a short coverage plan and goals doc before you go. I also recommend a weekly async check-in during weeks 3 and 6 so reintegration is smooth.

kai: Thanks all. One last: where do I send the signed docs? Email or via portal?

sam (People Ops): Submit forms to people-ops@redwood.com and upload scans to the HR portal if you prefer. Use subject line: "Parental Leave - kai - 2026-08" so payroll/benefits routing is automatic. We'll reply within 2 business days with next steps.

toni (Benefits): I'll follow up with an email that lists required docs and enrollment links.

kai: Perfect, really appreciate it :heart:

sam (People Ops): Congrats again! We'll monitor and help with any timing edge cases.

hr-bot: Reminder: add dependent within 30 days to avoid coverage gaps.

kai: Opening the form now.
